title: Caleb Williams on growing as a quarterback, comfort level in offense | Press Conference
text: Ben said the passing game has looked cleaner and, in particular, you've been very connected with Luther Coston and Rome more regularly. What were some of the factors that helped us find them? Yes, I think it's simply the consistency of having been able to have these guys , um, for the last two years, almost two years. Um, with Rome three, so, you know, I think that's important, communication;   I think our relationship as a group has grown. Um, we hang out together, we do things together, we eat together, we share bread, all that stuff;  And so, you begin to build that relationship, you know, that bond between us.  And , um, obviously, you know, they're super talented, so my job is simply to put the ball in their zone, um, and try to make the best pass, the best I can, every time. Yes, well, in the last few days since Monday night, your command of the line of scrimmage has been something of an highlight. What do you think has been the case? Has something been different for you, or has it simply been more noticeable, or do you feel a little more confident? What is it? Uh, same thing.   It was simply the noisy environment in which we had just played, so the communication, you know, maybe seemed a little more emphasized.  Uh, I'd say just this week or last week in general. Um, just knowing the environment, having played in some noisy matches before in my career, so, um, I think that's what came across .  But, uh , we communicate, and I think that's one of the most important things as an offense, being able to communicate. Um, and that doesn't waver depending on whether it's at home or visiting, you know, with a crazy crowd or not, so I think that's what it was. When you were out with the hamstring problem, did Ben talk today about how crucial you've been since you came back? Was that something you had in mind during those three games, like: when I come back I want to be more decisive? Yes, yes, that's what I thought, coming back, to simply be better overall, to place the ball better. Um, you know, be more decisive. Um, I think it's something I keep reminding myself of .  I've insisted on it, um , you know, ever since I was with Coach Riley.  Um, it's one of the last things we used to say to each other, um, in our QB meetings when I was, you know, with him: be decisive, be decisive, be decisive, be decisive.  And that's why , um, I think that's where it all comes from.  I think one of the most important things as a QB is to be decisive . Uh, when you have doubts and stuff like that, you know, you know, bad things happen.  So, uh, the decision wins is, is the motto I follow.  And, um, I just try to improve on that every single day. Caleb, since Caleb, since your return, you guys haven't been down in any of the three games.  All victories. I know you're looking ahead, but can you put into perspective how well they 've played in the last few weeks? Yes, a shout-out to the defense, uh, because there are times when we haven't started with the ball. Um, and then, a shout-out to the offensive line and wide receivers, and everyone just doing their job.  I think that's what it all boils down to Uh, we knew that, like last week , they're not a defense that, you know , normally allows explosive plays and, you know, a first scoring attack. And so, um, I think it was important for us to be able to go out there and have some energy whenever we had the ball, whether it was, you know, in the first series or, you know, after them. for us to go out there, execute, you know, put the ball in the guys' hands, uh, gain those three, four, you know, yards, uh, maybe some tough twos sometimes, and just try to stay the course. Um, and then from there, just play together, communicate, and do it well. It seems that the reaction to you outside of Chicago is a whiplash.  I mean, just in the summer, uh, America couldn't get enough of you.  Then everyone criticized you for overreacting to the injury.  And now you're, now you're back on top , uh, publicly.  Do you get motivation from both extremes? No. People, people will say what they have to say.  I can't please everyone .  That, that's not my job .  My job is to go out and win games. My job is, uh, to be the best player I can be. My job is to believe in myself, trust my teammates, and go out there and be one of those guys on the field who makes game- changing plays.  So , whether you like it or not, you have to accept it. I saw that you posted a picture of a Hacker or a sign on your social media. Yes, yes. I mean, do you like it, do you enjoy watching that kind of thing? That's fun.  Sometimes, you know, when you get into games and, you know, other players have said it.  When you go into games and you only need one thing or, um, maybe that was it. Yes, but Ben talks about the day after a game, about leaving success or failure behind.  He wants all those meetings to be the same, whether it's a victory or a defeat.  And how do you feel that atmosphere is in relation to what Ben wants? And how do you see your teammates accepting that message of continuing to improve? Yes, I think that actually when we win , sometimes our meetings are much tougher than when we lose. As I always say, good games or victories hide the truth. They hide the bad things.  And so, I think, I think that's what we are.  That is our identity. When, you know, whether it's good or bad, we're going to be hard on ourselves. We are going to evaluate ourselves rigorously.  And we're going to tell the truth about who we are, what we're doing, what we're doing right and what we're not doing. In those long offensive series, do you feel like you have to be perfect because the more plays you make, the greater the chance that something will go wrong ? No. I don't feel that way. I think when you start having those long runs, it's just a matter of finding complete passes.   It's about keeping the offensive series alive.  It's not about going out to kill, so to speak.  It's not about looking for the long shot.  In other words, well, the long shot isn't there.  Let's make a short pass.  We're going to gain those 4 or 5 yards.  Uh, and and and keep the offensives alive.  I think that's where we've grown as an offense. Whether it's, you know, me finding someone, you know, giving the ball to a teammate and him running through, and you know , getting those extra 2 yards, or well, it's just me being able to find a quick short pass, uh, and stuff like that. And from there, we move the ball, we move it well.  That's part of who we are.  It's, you know, a big part of who we are.  So, uh, we're going to keep doing that.  We'll keep looking for short passes and then, uh, when the explosive plays appear, when the opportunities arise, we'll take advantage of them too.  Do those offenses somehow emulate or , I suppose, highlight your growth in seeing the short pass and not necessarily looking for the pinpoint hit? Do you feel that 's an area where you've grown? Yes. Yes, I would say I've grown in that area. I think, uh, if you go back to high school, all I did was try for long plays.  I went to university and ran around with the ball a bit .  I made a few short passes, very few. And then, you know, my first year was very short.  I was really captivated, all of that.  And then last year, or, uh, yes, last year, I found a few more, although I kept running a bit. Uh, and then, you know, this year I've felt a lot more comfortable with, you know, my, you know, playbook and, uh , understanding it and, you know, what we want to do with certain plays.  And then, you know, from there, being able, uh , when we don't get specific cover, just being able to make the short pass and keep the offense alive. Yes, on that topic, when you see yourself in the recording of the last three games, do you realize how different you look as a player, how different you look as a quarterback compared to the beginning of your career?   Uh , no.   I mean , I still had a couple of pretty good getaways, I'd say. Uh, so, I still, I still do all that .  I think, uh, I wouldn't say I look different.  I think I've simply grown in certain aspects.  I think I've tried to maintain the things I've done well.  And then, you know, the things I have n't done well, I just try to bring them up to the level of, you know, the other things I have done well.  So , uh, I wouldn't say otherwise.  I think part of it is simply comfort with the offensive, too. I think that's a very important part, uh, on my end. And then, uh, just find a way to keep pushing myself and try to be better for the guys. Perhaps in that sense, Ben spoke about taking yourself out of your comfort zone and being receptive to new things, even if you don't like a particular play. Being outside your comfort zone, what does that mean to you? Yes. That's it, that's how you grow, that's how you improve.  I think, you know, sometimes you're in the middle of the season and, uh, you want to execute things that maybe suit you a little more or something, and then we practice a few times and stuff like that.  And you know, I obviously trust Ben with that So, you know, when he asks for something and I do n't like it, we go to the office, we sit down, we talk about it, he shows me videos, and if I still don't like it, or you know, I still don't see it or something, he won't ask for it, because that, you know , is like ruining, you know, ruining me out there And he is, he is, he's great at that. But a lot of times, you know, we go to the office, we talk about it, we watch multiple, multiple, multiple videos, and at the end of that, I usually feel pretty good about it and where we want to move the ball. Well, the Buccaneers have had a total of six interceptions in the last two weeks.  They have limited their opponents to 13 points and zero points respectively in the last matches What do you think is contributing to this increase in their defense? Yes, I think I mean, I think getting your man back, your leader back, getting Baker back, I think that was part of it. He is a great source of energy for them throughout their entire playing career, from when I saw him in college until now.  I think that, that has been important for him in the teams he has been a part of , and then I think, I think that as the season progresses, you get into a rhythm. Um, you find your rhythm, you discover what works well, you discover what doesn't and then you make corrections, and I think they've done a good job with that and they're playing well defensively, they move all over the field. Um, I think that's probably the biggest factor in why they can play so well, especially on defense. Sorry, sorry for interrupting. Jason Larry, Jason. Good. More or less on the topic of short weeks, and, you know, are you new here? Okay, I understand.  Yes, we just, just , yes, yes, okay, okay, okay, okay, sorry. Yes, you're a good guy.  What's happening? In the last year and a half or so since Ben joined the team, yes, short weeks at the end of...you guys have won these last six games where there's good.   With a week between two games, whether it's because of your procedure or the way Ben simplifies things during the week, how can you achieve balanced success? Yes. Uh, I think it's just...Uh, first, Ben's been doing this for a while. Uh, and then, and then, you know, for my part, I think that just...Uh, time management is fundamental. Um, and so, being able to arrive early , stay late, um, define your routine early and, you know, in these short weeks and in the long weeks, just figure out what works for you.  I think that's important and then, um, you know, just constantly immersing yourself in the plays.  Um, that's it , that's important in short weeks, because teams are going to throw a lot at you.  Um, they're going to run their things and they're going to, you know, have things planned for you as usual.  Um, so, knowing your material, obviously, you know, you might not end up studying that much video, but you try to review as much as you can.  Um, and then, and then, from there, as I said, you study your material extremely hard and extremely well.  Um, you know, so when you get to the, when you get to the game, you feel extremely comfortable with, you know, whatever is going to happen.  You know, you know where your short passing options are.  You know where your hot routes are.  You know your alerts.  You know your "kills".  You know why we're eliminating them.  Uh, you know, and then from there it's just a matter of going out and throwing a good pass. The trade for Jeffery Simmons really seemed to create excitement in the building.  What have you felt, both on and off the field, about adding someone like that?  I know I saw you excited about defending on the wing. Yes, yes.  It is, uh. He has been the best defensive tackle in recent years, if not number one, then number two.  And, I would say number one.  Well, having a player who makes a difference like that makes everyone's job easier.  Uh, I'm referring to the energy it provides.  Uh, I've played against him, so the provocations and all that.  And well, you know, it's fun having him on our side, and also, the leadership aspect.  Obviously, we haven't, you know, immersed ourselves, he immersed himself in his work.  I immersed myself in my work last week after he arrived here.  But anyway, it was just a small example, you know, later and he wasn't here.  I spoke to the boys and told them, "Let's make sure we clean up."   Let's take care of our people. Uh, and he wasn't there when I said it, and you know, one of the first things he does after the game is clean up, and you know, he's an All-Pro guy.   It's this and that.  I mean, he could leave and nobody would say anything.  Nobody would care, and he cleaned the entire locker room, both the offensive and defensive sides.  So that's who he is, and I'm happy to have him on our side. You know, he's going to help the lads, I sincerely believe he's going to lead them and make them better, and I think Monday was a prime example of that. The last one. I also had a question about Jeffery Simmons.  I was wondering if you had time—this is just a guess since it's only been a week—but did you actually have time to talk to him? Did you? About what? About anything.  How to get to know him a little better.   I have n't had much time with the team together. Yes, yes.  No, I haven't had much time to do that yet. Uh, I don't know much about him obviously and all that, and well, it's the same for him, but now we're on the same team and, you know, we're going to have a laugh. Let's joke around.  Let's, you know, smile.  At some point we'll all hang out , but for now we're focused.  We're trying to move this forward.  So maybe during the break, if he's in town, we'll hang out, you know, a group of us.  That's what we usually do if everyone is in the city or a group of people, but if not, we'll look for another time.  He's going to be here for a while.  So we will continue to move forward. Incredible. The best.

title: Exclusive Interview with Tyson Campbell
text: Welcome back to Cleveland Browns Daily, brought to you by Bally Bet, the official sports betting partner of your Cleveland Browns.  And I'm very pleased to have with us today someone who is quickly becoming a great friend of this program, Browns cornerback Tyson Campbell.  And Tyson, obviously, the result in Pittsburgh wasn't what we wanted as a team. How do you all feel about it?  Saying, " Look, we're still in a good position, 5 and 3."  We turn the page and prepare for the Saints. Yes, simply be grateful to know that you have another opportunity to get rid of that bad taste in your mouth, correct your mistakes, and improve on last week. So that's our mindset. Coming here with a new game plan, correcting our mistakes from last week, and hopefully finishing week 1-0. Well, I would say on the outside of our defense, at the cornerback position, there weren't many mistakes last week.  They tried you a couple of times and you said, "no, thanks," covering those Mr. Metcalf routes. Five passes directed towards you, you allowed one reception for 4 yards. That's pretty good.  I was talking to Denzel a while ago, I told them that between the two of them, they threw the ball nine times I think in the game and allowed 12 yards in total .  That's incredibly elite.  How good did you feel in that game with what you were doing out there, especially when they looked for you one-on- one? Oh, yes, brother.  I knew that's what they were going to do, you know what I mean ?  Try to run with the ball and then throw your passes to the outside.  So, lots of video study during the week , following receiver trends, and when the game came, it was easy.  Once I was able to read their movements, I was able to react to them . How different was it for you?  Because I remember that your first game with the Cleveland Browns was in that stadium. You arrived here, I think on a Wednesday or a Thursday, and you played on Sunday.  Now, a year later, how different is everything and how different was that experience before going out onto the field? Definitely a moment that brings things full circle, you know. I was much quieter in that locker room compared to this year, where , you know, I practically know the guys.  So yes, it was a moment that brings things full circle, no doubt, although I wish we had taken the victory. And we're, you know, 1 and 1 against them .  They divided the series into seasons.  There you have it, 2 and 1 in the division right now .  Now we're going to New Orleans to face the Saints.  They're coming off a week's break, so they'll be rested.  They have one of the best young wide receivers in the NFL, Chris Olave.  How have you seen them in terms of your preparation to face this team? Yes, it's a young group with quarterback Taysom Hill and, as you said, a group of young receivers who like to make explosive plays and work in open spaces.  So it's going to be, you know, a fun showdown.  I can't wait. I hope, you know, there's a lot of competition.  Do you like playing cornerback? Do you prefer being in the indoor stadium or outside? I like being outside in the grass. OK. But you know, I played in the Sugar Bowl twice That's what I was going to say, yes, yes. So I'm familiar with that stadium.  So yes, there's obviously a lot of history in that stadium.  It is a unique stadium in the sense that the fans are very far from the field on the sidelines.  It's almost as if you were all isolated there .  Yes. You like it because you can concentrate better, right? Yes, no, definitely.  I mean, anyway, I do n't really listen to the fans much during the game .  Yes, so once you 're on the field, you feel like you and that person are the only ones there.  So when you think about how you and Denzel have developed as a couple.  We had the great Carson Swash and the current Defensive Rookie of the Year come by and say that we have two number one cornerbacks.  And that's really it, that's what I think about it.  That's what many people think about it.  You know, I told you before that Andrew Berry said you 're probably the most underrated player on this roster.  You won't be underestimated for long if you keep going out there and giving the performances you're giving.  But how does it feel to know that you and Denzel are out there, two guys on the wings who can block opponents? Oh yeah, it's a blessing, man.  And the only thing we can do is, you know, keep helping each other improve Tell each other what we see and learn different things from one another.  And I feel that , you know, God continues to bless us with good health.  You know, we're capable of doing something special. Yes, speaking of that slightly scary moment when you had to quit the game.  What happened in that play and how did you know you were okay?  I'm back. Yes, just a small bump on the neck. Yes. And, of course, I had to go through the whole protocol before they let me go out again .  But I'm fine now.  So, good. Ready to move forward.  Yes. Yes, ready to move forward.  Yes. And so far, this is a team that has shown great resilience, right? We lost the first week in Jacksonville, then we won three in a row.  We lost against the Jets. We won a couple in a row after that. How have you seen this team's resilience after this game? Yes, man.  Like you said, don't get too excited or get discouraged. Take it week by week, be where your feet are and know where we are. We're playing the New Orleans Saints and the goal is to win, so that's all that matters to us. Very good.  Well, you and I have been talking about something that's happening at the university level that's coming up.  We're just passing through.  Deuce Staley is already talking about a couple of weeks. Georgia, my daughter in South Carolina, is coming soon.  South Carolina doing its job.  Maybe they'll manage to do this. I hope they do it in a big way.  Perhaps College Game Day will appear. That would be good.   It would be a great showdown, man.   It's always fun to play in that stadium, to see the fans making sandstorms, seeing the towels and things like that.  So, a great university experience indeed. For someone like me, this will be my first SEC game, and I'm sure there are a lot of people watching who may have never had the joy of being at a big SEC football game.  What makes it so special? In the South, they live, breathe, and die for American football, so that's what you're going to feel. You're going to feel an atmosphere full of passion and determination, and that will give you goosebumps, so you're sure to enjoy it. Many people say that in Cleveland, just like you said, they live for the Cleveland Browns.  This is one of the few places where you feel that kind of similar vibe.  Obviously the weather isn't that great, but you can feel that same vibe. No, definitely not.  I would say it's something I noticed quickly when I arrived here - rain, sleet, snow, the Dawg Pound always appears week after week, so they are definitely die- hard fans here. Excellent.  Very good.  Well, good luck this week.  Have a great week of training.  Go to New Orleans , achieve your goal, get back on the winning track, and it's always fun to talk to you and see you go out on the field to close down spaces. That's right, sir.  I apreciate it. Very good.  Tyson Campbell, our guest.  We'll be back with more from Cleveland Browns Daily, presented by Bally Bet, right after this.

title: NFL Trade Deadline Show: Who Should Buffalo Bills Target? | Always Gameday in Buffalo
text: 123, 123 >> HEY Bills Mafia, we know there's one thing on your mind everyday. Your team, the Buffalo Bills. So Matt Bove and Sal Capaccio are here to bring you the latest news, notes, and opinions straight from the source, right here, right now. Because it's always game day in Buffalo. >> [music] >> We have not yet been traded, Matt Bove. Sal Capaccio, we are here. It is trade deadline week, I guess. I mean, so so we're recording this on on Tuesday. Matt's like, we got to do a trade deadline episode. I'm like, you're right, because what's going to happen is next Monday, Matt, the Bills are going to play in Minnesota, and then Tuesday is the trade deadline. So everything's going to come very quickly. >> Yeah, I mean, theoretically, they could just trade for Justin Jefferson right after the game. He could come back to Buffalo on the team plane. So if they want to do that, logistically, it would be a lot easier that way. But yeah, no, I'm glad we're doing this. I did want to do something because it feels like once we get later into this week, it's going to be about the Bills and the Vikings, and rightfully so. It's a big game. It's going to be about is Carson Wentz going to play? Is Kyler Murray going to play? Like he popped up with an injury in the end of their last game, Kyler Murray, the Viking starting quarterback. It'll be about, hey, is DJ Moore ready to go? What about Spencer Brown? So it's like, okay, we're recording this on Tuesday, election day, November 3rd, 1 week away from the deadline. They could make a deal now, right? Like they could make a deal before the deadline. Like they've done it before. I do think though, the reason I wanted to do this, I think they're going to do something. Now, it doesn't have to be trade multiple first-round picks, Jeffrey Simmons, massive splash. But I think this team realizes, Brandon Beane realizes, they're 6 and 1, they control their own destiny right now. There's not like an absolute juggernaut in the AFC. Put the chips in the middle of the table and go for it. Do you agree? >> Yes, I do. I think they're going to do something. When you say put the chips in the middle of the table and go for it, I don't expect that to happen as far as like some massive blockbuster, but you never know. I mean I know fans hate when Brandon Bean Brandon Bean brings up the salary cap constraints and things like that, but you know, that is how he has operated. So and that is a reality of life having a salary cap. You know, the Bills have made a few deals over the last few years. Amari Amari Cooper and Na'im Hines come to mind. And these are the kinds of deals you'd probably expect something like this, right? Like you you maybe trade a draft pick and a guy that can help you. Although in both cases, to different degrees, I mean Na'im Hines came in and became a a decent kick returner, but he never got integrated in the offense. Um Amari Cooper came in, he got hurt actually, and he never really got integrated in the offense as you know, you wanted him to. So these things, you never know where they're going to go. Jaylen Waddle last year getting traded to the Denver Broncos never really made an impact for the Denver Broncos to be quite honest with you, right? I mean >> Well, Jaylen Waddle Jaylen Waddle didn't get traded till the middle of the of the summer. >> Oh oh, I'm sorry. I'm sorry. That's right. Um sorry. Sauce Sauce Gardner went Sauce Gardner went Quinnen Williams went like there were some trades that were made last year. Um and I have to remember exactly when those were, but anyway, I guess that you never know how these things are going to go. Then you see the other side of it where Jeffrey Simmons made a huge impact last night Monday night football >> the Chicago Bears. >> Yeah, I think so, too. I just think like Amari Cooper is a good cautionary tale that he got here and he made some plays, but then he got banged up and it was never like the level of impact that they were hoping for. I don't think that this team is going to make a huge huge huge splash, but I could see them trading multiple draft picks for multiple players in an effort to try and help their team. And I think that they could be impactful players. So the exercise we're going to do is we both wrote down we texted each other five different players that we think the Bills could or should be targeting before the deadline. Now, our lists would overlap. Like there are guys who Sal picked who I would absolutely Like one of the guys on Sal's list, I think is the most likely outcome for really the entire thing for the Bills. >> Okay. >> I've got a couple other guys that are a little different. So yeah, like that's going to be the exercise we do. We each go over these five guys. >> And and we're going to do that in a second. I do want to get to one thing that it's interesting when I think about this. The greatest trade ever for the Bills, I think, happened in 1987 on Halloween night when they traded for Cornelius Bennett. And it's one of the greatest trades in NFL history, actually. Now, granted, they they never did win a Super Bowl, but on Halloween night 1987, the Buffalo Bills traded for Cornelius Bennett. And I want to throw up on the screen if people You want to talk about blockbuster, Matt? I don't know if you know cuz you weren't alive then, of course. >> Mhm. >> Here's what happened. The Buffalo Bills traded for Cornelius Bennett, who was a holdout at the time from the Indianapolis Colts. He was a top pick. He was a like third pick overall, I think. They traded a very good running back, Greg Bell, along with two first-rounders and a second-rounder. Okay? The Colts traded The Colts then traded uh for Eric Dickerson in this trade. It's a three-team deal. A first-round Look, anyway, just look at the screen, folks. You got Bennett, you got two firsts, you got a second, another second, a running back named Owen Gill, uh more draft picks involved. It was insane. This was an amazing trade, and I always think about this trade and like, "Oh my god, we never We don't see things like that anymore, really." >> How was this received when it happened? Because in 1987, you know, it was right before the Bills kind of started to go on their run. So like that would have been a really premium price to pay before kind of fully arrived. Were people excited about this? Were people apprehensive? Like how did it >> So, what's funny is you say that, and I remember listening to John Murphy on WBEN, and he was totally against it. He's like, "You don't trade that much for a for a outside linebacker. You don't trade that much for Like that is way too much to give up, and I don't know if this team is, you know, in a position to be able to do that." But obviously it worked out. I mean, the Bills went to four Super Bowls and we look back at it as one of the greatest trades ever. So, I think there were mixed results and mixed views. He came in like the first game he played, he made a huge impact with sacking the quarterback. There was a lot of stuff that happened. I mean, right away Bennett, you knew like, "Oh my god, they actually got a player here and they did this." But, I mean, to give up two first and a second and a thousand-yard rusher in Greg Bell. That time was amazing actually to think about. >> So, did they have and excuse my ignorance here, so did they have Greg Bell and Thurman Thomas? >> No, Greg Bell got traded the year after they traded for Bennett. They drafted Thurman. They had no first-round pick. >> In the second round. >> Because of the trade and they drafted Thurman in the second round. That's right. >> Okay, that's interesting. Yeah, wow. Does the amount of like stars on that team is that's the one of the things that's I got off on a tangent. That team was loaded with stars. >> Oh, yeah. >> This team is Josh Allen, James Cook, and then some good players. But, like not even close to the star power that those teams back in the day had, which is crazy. >> Yeah, I mean, we've talked before about not having the all-pro talent, but having a little more of the floor and you'd love to see maybe the Bills have some of those guys that really put them over the top, which is why we're doing this exercise here today. All right, so Matt and I gave some names to each other. You want to start off? You want to You want to give me a name on your list? >> I think I want actually you to start because the seg- the conversation we just had, um I think sets up nicely for you have one name that I think is definitely better than the other nine names total. Like that would be the most expensive, the most impactful, the biggest splash. So, why don't we start with that? >> And I'm guessing [clears throat] you're talking about the third guy I gave you, right? So, I know. So, I'm going to just going to do it here. I want you to say who it is, so I know. >> Max Crosby. >> Oh, okay. Well, it's interesting that you chose him because I debated not even putting on my list and here's why. >> The Raiders are four and four. >> Yeah. >> They're a game out of a wild card. I don't think they're trading Max Crosby, folks. Different mindset, different energy, like anything like that? Our team came out today ready to work and they showed that on Monday we went out to practice. So, it's been really great intent, very deliberate practice from everybody. I really love the love the energy, love the execution, love how guys are operating. So, I'm excited to see how we continue to progress this week and keep the great practices going. One day is okay. Can we do it consecutive days and can all of that translate to Sunday? >> What are you seeing from the Chargers? um teams that are 0 and seven it can be kind of sneaky dangerous because they're probably better than that. What are you seeing and what do you how do you guard against that? >> As I look at the Chargers is their team is it you know is definitely not indicative of their record like they are really good football team. Quarterback's a really great player and their defense has been really good. Their defense is stout on third down. They eliminate the explosives. So this is a really good team. We don't come in looking at the record and making any, you know, pre-etermined notions of who this team is. Like, we go out, we watch the film, we prepare for a really good team. They're very, uh, intricate offense. They move guys around a lot. Have a lot of things that can get your eyes if you're not careful. Uh, Mike does a really good job of scheming that in the run. I think they they'll stick to the run and we have to do a great job of defending the run. uh some issues that we had in the previous week of not defending the run well there late in the football game. It's the same thing this week. We got to defend it for four quarters, right? And we do that, you know, we feel that'll be one of the keys to this game, but we also understand Herbert and his abilities to make plays, especially him in the pocket and haven't seen a quarterback who, as tough as he is in a pocket, be able to shake defenders off and still complete the ball downfield. So, we got to do a great job of rushing together as a unit with our four guys and we got to do a great job in coverage as well. >> With Jaylen being out, will we see more increased snaps for Tank this week? >> Yeah, we'll see more of Tank and not not because of who's out, which is Tank. This is his second week now uh playing. So, I think his reps will just increase with his workload. He's put a lot of work in on the side and just natural progression of an increase in his workload. those same mindset you've been able to see um improvement as far as learning the playbook, getting familiar with CJ from Marvin Harrison Jr. >> Marvin has done a great job since the first day he's gotten here when it comes to learning the playbook. Marvin's a really smart player. He's picked up on everything fairly quickly. Uh he's he's been attentive and he's been dialed in, studying a lot, so he's he's very well verssed in the playbook. >> Any updates on David McGomery? Um his his health progress? >> David is still, you know, sideline. He'll he'll be out. We're still, you know, we trying to get him on the field, trying to get him going, but right now it's still week to week, but he has made some progress. >> Having a healthier Aziz Alire, how much can that boost the defense when he's healthier? Just seems to move a lot better and seems to give you guys a boost. >> Defensively, we have to play together. Like, whoever is out there, one guy, everybody to be healthy flying around. Of course, everybody is their best when they're they're feeling good. So that's, you know, for all of our guys, we want them, they should be flying around feeling good after the by-week, the much needed rest that we were able to receive. I expect to see a renewed energy in our group on Sunday. >> Oh, aside from tackling jobs worked on, what adjustments that you feel comfortable sharing, have you all made on the defensive side to try to uh get to where you all hope you all can reach? For us defensively, we just got to go play our defense the right way. It's playing with fundamentals, playing with technique, everybody playing together. That's good defensive football. So, it's not a ton of adjustments that need to be made. We just got to go out and play it the right way. >> You put emphasis on the fact that you want your offensive lineman to be more physical in the run game. Will we see any type of different lineups heading into the charges or will you still roll out that same group? >> Our same group will go out there. talk about finishing being a key kind of what happens up front. Are you seeing any signs of them being able to do that better? It's game time. >> It's all good on Wednesday, right? [laughter] It all looks good on Wednesday and throughout the week. But as you [clears throat] all know, it's about game day, right? And our guys, they know what to do. They know how to do it. It's a matter of doing that consistently for those 65 snaps that we're going to get on Sunday. And that's what I'm most excited to see. Like our finish, how we how we go about our business uh against a really good front. The Chargers defensive line, they don't get enough credit. They have very good guys up front who play disruptive. They can make plays in the back field. Good rushers off the edge with Tuli, with Max. So, we got our hands full again as every week. And so, our guys will get tested this week. When it comes to that challenge of how you finish, you have to outwork these guys up front because they'll do a good job of mixing up their starts, games, moving around. So, we got to do a great job of outworking and finishing up front. >> What you seen? You know, obviously the tech you guys have started 205. How have you seen your guys, your players [clears throat] together amidst, you know, disappointing start, but how you seen them stick together? >> It's only one way forward and that's together. I haven't seen any I haven't seen it any other way. Our guys have been very good. Our game they they've been close games. So guys see those couple plays where we've been off. Now the focus, our mindset is on how do we just finish. It's not about staying together. Our guys been together. That's that's never a message or it's nothing that I have to talk about. It's just how do we play better football and finish. >> The Rams game against the Chargers. What were some things you see from they looked like they were trying to anticipate a lot of Herbert throws. They looked like they had a lot of upfield rush. they were able to shoot a lot of gaps against them. The >> Rams, they did a good job. They again, that ball game was tight there at the half. You know, before they were able to get a couple turnovers to flip the game, you know, in their favor. So, when I look at that game and I look at all of the Chargers games, I don't look at the record. I watch the tape and this these games have been close just like all games in the NFL. They're talented football team. They're competitive. Coach Harbaugh teams have always been competitive and that's what he's known for. They're going to be physical. We just got to find a way to continue to outwork them as best we can. We know it's going to be a challenge four quarter battle. Uh and we got to find a way to finish it. >> What do you want the run game to be? >> I want us to move the football. Run, pass, it doesn't matter. I want us to move the football and score points. >> All right. Thank you. the energy on Monday. >> Yeah, I think the energy is great. Everybody's refreshed. Everybody's ready to go. And I think, man, we're just itching for that next op. And it shows today in practice. I thought we flew we flew around. Everybody was getting to the ball. Offense looked really good. defense looked really good. Um, everybody is just like we're ready just to go play now. You know what I'm saying? I think the B week was really good for everybody. So, it's I'm glad to have everybody back in the building. It's It's been good. So, since we've been back. >> How was your your buy and what are your expectations? >> Yeah, the B was good. I think it was just a mental reset. Get your body back right. Take some time for yourself. Reflect. Um, before we left, you know, coach asked us to reflect, you know, how we played the first few games, areas that we can get better at. Um, and what was the second part of your question? Um what are your expectations particularly of the defense? >> Yeah. Uh go back to our standard. I think like I said like reflecting watching the tape it's just we have to do a better job of swarming. We have to do a better job of leaning in on our foundation and I think that's just been the biggest reflection like are we playing our branded ball on tape on a consistent level? >> You're true. >> Yeah. >> Why do you think that you can just start playing swarm all of a sudden? >> Yeah. I mean it's it's not going to happen overnight but I think the more you practice it, the more reps you get, the more consistent you be at it during the week. it's going to show up on Sunday and that's just how football is. Like you never know when it's going to show up but it's going to show up eventually and I feel like we have the guys to do it. We have a really great team and you go back and watch those games, it just come down to finishing. It comes down to how consistent can you be at the end of the game. I mean we're not getting blown out. The scores have been like right there by each other. So I think for us is looking at that in a positive way. It's like man if we can just finish these games and just continue to play our brand of ball consistent for four quarters going into overtime we would have been in a much better spot. But we have 10 games that we have to do that and there's no negotiation for that. >> Has talked consistently about tackling tackles. How do you all plan to clean that up coming out of the B? >> Yeah. So today he took us back to pee ball today. He had all of us line up on the 35 yard line in the line and one person was on their knees, other person was standing up and you stay here and you drive and wrap and squeeze and then you got up stand up five yards apart go tackle the man drive for five. But um you know whatever it takes to get the job done. You know what I'm saying? like you know football was played differently back then and how it is now and so like he's reting us like no you got to go put your body on people like you just can't go to the side and just jump off the diving board and just think a arm tackle is going to work in this league like you got to put body on body so I think that's an area that you know we continue to clean up and get these guys on the ground >> being at the level you guys are is that going through that you talk about it's pee-wee ball is that >> you know I don't want to put a word to it I want you to explain is it annoying is it frustrating is it what kind of emotions No, it's fun, man. This is football is fun. Like, you don't make it bigger than what it is. You don't go out and look for a negative reason to say, "Oh, we're doing this stupid." Like, no. Like, that's what football is. No matter what level is like, you go when a rookie comes in, you tell them, "Man, it's just it's just ball. You've been playing ball your whole life." And that's what it is. It's just ball. You go out there, you do what the coach tell you to do, and if that's what he wants us to do, we're going to go out there and have joy and do it. Like, nobody's complaining about it. It was fun. Like, but that's the type of stuff that we do to continue to rally behind each other, continue to have the camaraderie that we have with stuff like that. Like that was even though we may laugh at it, but that's a good chemistry drill for us. Like even though we're working on getting better, like it just take you back to those days when you first started playing football, like yes, it's a serious drill, but that's what makes it light and that's what makes everybody want to continue to come to work in this building and continue to show up and play. >> Well, you guys had some success in the past against Chargers and Justin playing the playoff game. What do you see from him this year and some ways that you've seen defenses successfully attack him so far this year? >> Yeah, he's still a really great quarterback in this league. You talk about a big guy who has a big arm that can run around, that can throw the ball deep, makes a lot of plays with his legs, he's still, you know, a very respectable player in this league and we have a ton of respect for them. Um, as far as scheme, you know, we're going to probably see a lot of bounce. You know, uh, McDonald's, he's went against this defense a lot of times. Um, coached against this defense was at San Fran, I believe. So, um, we know what to expect a little bit, but Herbert, man, he's playing out his mind. They have a really great solid O line as well and some really good running backs that can get downhill, that can hit the perimeter. So, it's going to be a good challenge for us. a couple of times that there's like small margin for error on this defense. >> Can you emphasize what that what does that mean? >> Tackling, doing your job, communicating. Like those are non-negotiables that we can't have. You know what I'm saying? Like you play defense, we got to tackle better. You play defense, we got to communicate better. So like those are just things that we can't have an area that's those are bad in you. where you said that you all have 10 games left and I know that you all are taking it one game at a time but do you still feel that the postseason is a possibility for you all? >> Yeah, most definitely. Most definitely. But I just I think where we at right now like we have to take it one day at a time, one game at a time. Like we can't look too far ahead. Like we know what we want as a team. We know the goals that we want, but I think right now it's like each week how doubt in how detailed can I be on this one opponent to go out and do my job to the best of my ability and just to win these next games to get to where we want to be at. When you look at the record, it is what it is right now. Tendency could be to go out there as as players >> and almost try to do too much to make that play and >> get out of the detail side of it and just doing your job, whatever the players, what's the message in that with that regard going into this? >> Yeah. Um, I don't I think for us is like it's so weird being in this position because it's I haven't felt the energy of anybody trying to press and overdo their job or like even talking in the locker room like we haven't been like oh we got to go press and it's just like man like just go do your job like do what's required of you and that's on all phases each level like up front back in middle guys just like nobody's pressing to go make a play that's not theirs. So I think for us it's just we're looking at it just more as man like how well again can you do can I do my job on a consistent basis for us to win these games. So I don't really think it's like anybody going to press to go make a play or anything like that. It's just bro lean back in on your foundation. You know who we are as a team what coach do has br here the culture that we have set here. Lean back in on that. And I think that's what makes us great is we have a foundation. We have a we we have a great squad that knows what to do. We just have to continue to put it together and be one. >> How good does it feel to get that going back? It feels good. Big Mark Henry. [laughter] >> No, it's great to have him back, man. He He He brings a lot of light to that room for us, man. He He's really great for us up front. I thought he had a really great preseason for us. And to have him back in his room, it felt like, you know, he he's been there. You know, we love him. Glad to have him back. He's going to make a lot of plays for us. How much does his impact help you guys when it comes to just whether it's stopping the run or just the just the size of him as >> Yeah, just another big body in the middle that can clog up the hole, get some of these backers free, scraping downhill, taking up space uh to continue to eliminate this run game. So, having him back is really huge for us. >> You said coach to reflect during during the by-week. How do you reflect? Do you meditate? Do you journal? Do you read? How do you approach? >> Yeah. Um for me, I love fishing. So, I just got on the boat and I didn't even catch on fish. It was just more so of just a reset of just being out on the water and just, you know, calming myself down and, you know, really just recentering myself and remembering who I am. You know what I'm saying? And not getting caught up in everything. So, I think for me is just going through my daily process of, you know, remembering the peace that I have, remembering who I am, how much hard work that I put in, and, you know, continue to go through my process. >> The struggles that you guys have gone through, it's new to you. How have you handled that just mentally as kind of alluded to, you know, as a human being. >> Yeah, most definitely. It's frustrating because that's a natural human, you know, emotion to have. But I think also as a leader, you have to keep the face of bringing energy every day, being a consistent guy, showing up even when you don't feel like it. And I think that's what makes great teams great is when they have guys like Aziz, they have guys like Petri, CJ, um, Nico that continue to show up every day and be that same guy, um, that people look at. And that's how a team continues to strive forward, no matter what your record is, is that when you look at the leaders on this team, how they coming into the building and how everybody receiving them. >> Appreciate it, guys. Y'all have a good one. Chargers, some of the things they do. How do you do that? How do you kind of compartmentalize and ignore what's happened so far and just kind of focus on, okay, how do you beat them? >> Well, you put on the tape, you know, I put on their tape and their defense, you know, they make plays. Um they make it really hard on some really good offenses they played um you know they played really good against the Bills, played really good against the Seahawks um against Denver, you know, so they they they played against some good offenses and done some good things. So you know it's NFL got great players, you know, every week. So got to be prepared. >> How does the loss of Jaylen Noah affect you all on offense? >> Yeah, I mean we're going to feel it. You know, he's been he was playing really great. Um took a big step, you know, from his rookie year to this year. Um, you know, I feel for him. I feel bad. You know, it sucks that, you know, you know, he's starting to really find himself and then to go down like that. But he's a tough, resilient kid and I know, you know, he has, you know, faith in God and faith in himself that, you know, he'll get through this. >> You talked a lot about in the past handling the ups and downs. People love you, people hate you, like whatever. Right now, everything's like super positive about you. How are you handling this maybe differently than your rookie year if there is a difference in how you're handling, you know, a lot of the praise you're getting? Uh, I really don't see it, so I don't know. Um, but it to me it really doesn't matter. Like in the flip of a coin, people can not like me again or think that I'm doing playing however. So, um, you know, I just try to focus on whatever's in front of me. You know, if that's a meeting, a walk through, a practice, and that's really where, you know, it's gotten me to where I'm at now to be playing well so far. So, um, but I know, you know, just a little distraction or a little unfocused, you know, tendencies can get you, you know, to not be playing well cuz sleep is that good. So really just trying to focus on one day at a time, one thing at a time and even if that's getting away from the building, you know, during the bye-week and focusing on that, enjoying myself and getting some free time, you know, did that. So now I'm back to work and now I'm focused on work. So um just being able to, you know, focus on what's in front. >> Assume sorry, assuming that is true that you don't see it, how hard is it? >> Well, you got to assume. Well, because everyone says they never see anything and we know that that's not always the case, but assuming you don't see it, like how hard is it to actively not seek it or like see it by accident? >> Uh, one, I tell family members and friends not to send it to me. Um, so that's not been a that hasn't been a problem over the last couple years. And then I'm really not on social media. Um, I logged in a little bit this this um um this uh by by week just to, you know, see if any family or friends. And I have some people who run my pages. So, um, but honestly, I don't I don't really look for it. Um, cuz it just social media is not real anyways. Everybody's posting their highlights. Like, I go through things every day. You know, I I have ups and downs that people don't see, you know, on and off the field. So, but no one's posting those things. So, I just don't I don't really relate to a lot of the things on social media. Um, not saying, you know, it doesn't have positive things as well. You know, I get a lot of my sermons and stuff on social media as well. So, um, or YouTube or whatever the case may be. So, it's not just all negative, but um I I I just don't think it it really like helps my life any better and it kind of helps me focus on what's important. That's, you know, where my feet are. >> Somebody make a comparison uh of like explosive pass plays to like three-point shot in basketball. And I'm I'm curious like as a quarterback, what does connecting on explosive plays uh do for you in particular? >> Yeah, I mean it lessens the drive, you know, um it makes the defense communicable. have all these explosives, you know, and then some things in the game will go wouldn't go right or we would have a three and out. And I just feel like even through those, you can still be aggressive. And I think Kale has done a great job, you know, and honestly, he's been very aggressive and I appreciate him, you know, trusting me with the ball. Um, and, you know, allowing me even to be able to make mistakes because I think sometimes when you're not being aggressive, you know, it's like you're you're not really like giving giving yourself a chance to, you know, um, push the ball down the field and whatnot. So thought, you know, we've been doing a great job and protection's been great, you know, and then I think it's the pass game's starting to open up the run a little bit, but you know, we got to be very we got to be more balanced as well. >> CJ, what do you see from the opportunity for Tank Dell going forward and now have these guys speedway and had a successful first game back and second part with Nico Collins? How tough is it sometimes to unlock him and get him going with the way the defenses are trying to cover him and pay a lot of attention to him? >> Yeah, I thought Tank did amazing. you know, I just thought the way he was able to control his emotions. You know, it's been, you know, a lot a lot of time from the last time he played a game and, you know, I thought he played really well. I know he didn't get a bunch of targets. Um, but, you know, his his role I think will pick up for us and, you know, he'll be able to, you know, start doing more for us and I think, you know, he today he had a great practice. Um, and you know, it's tough on Nick. You know, Nick is the guy. He's the number one. He's, you know, who everybody game plans for. So, uh, we got to find ways to get more creative. you know, just keeping them one spot, but also, you know, I think it's good for him, you know, to fight through some of the adversity and some of the, you know, the tough coverages. I I thought, you know, the Giants did a good job of trying to just be in our face all game and, you know, I think we're prepared for him better now. So, um, you know, I think he's a heck of a player, football player, I told him when I first met him, you know, I think he's going to be one of the best receivers ever play in this league, and he's been able to do that, you know, year in and year out. So, um, I think, you know, nothing the sky's is the limit for him, and, you know, he's going to keep going. in your fourth by week. What do you get out of a buy and how do you attack or approach the buy compared to the the first one and the [snorts] previous three? >> Uh yeah, you learn, you know, as a time kind of like offseason, you learn what to do, what not to do. Um so, you know, I think the best thing to do is just get your mind off it for a little bit. But before you do that, I think you should self scout, see where you can get better, then when you come back, do it again. You know, self scout again. And that's something that I did and you know, as a team, we did. We see where we can get better. and some of the the negative plays or penalties, why are we doing what we're doing? And then the good stuff that we're doing, how can we get better and how can we adapt and update and you know try to like uh create new explosive and new things to do. So um just a little bit of you know getting the work done on the front end, relaxing and then you know getting the work done on the back end as well. >> What did you do to get your mind off of football for those couple of days? I just relax, spend time with family, just chill >> from the Jacksonville game, the pass that you made to Woody late in the game and u I think if I'm not mistaken, it was Nick who said you and Woody were the ones who made the change as far as the jab or whatever the case may be on on that play. Is that just um describes how much control and how much you have taken over this playbook? Yeah, I think you know I've been able to you know come up with some cool things to show Kales and you know I think you know a lot of times when you're in systems um you know being coaches wise and you haven't really and I'm not saying this is something that they've done but a lot of times sometimes you can just stay in in the box of the system and I think they've done a great job of trying to see what we can do outside that box. Um, so just something like that, you know, something simple as that, uh, that you can get the backers to communicate in in a critical situation like that, you know, got us a big time first down and a, you know, to get us in field range for Kim to kick a game winner. Um, so yeah, I've been able to, you know, give a lot more input and, um, you know, we've been doing some cool things and I think it's not just me though. It's like, you know, Alex Ward, our, you know, our offensive line guy who's been giving good plays and Cole, same thing. Hassani, uh, TQ, you know, uh, a bunch of different people in the building who are in our ears and trying to help Kales and Kale's also coming up with creative things to do for us to, you know, be more explosive. So, um, I think stuff like that is great just to all be on one page. >> Can you talk about um, your relationship with Trent Brown and what a veteran like that means? Because when I talked to him earlier this week, he talked about he's kind of singing your praises, but he talked about how what he learns from you and I want to know what you learned from him. Yeah, TB is a vets vet and somebody who is, you know, a dog. Um, somebody I respected for a long time. Um, and just to have him as a teammate, like he's a great person, you know, he loves God, loves people. Um, you know, um, family man, you know, loves his kids. Um, I just I'm proud of him just how he's brought along uh like Fabeti and Taye and Blake and all these different guys in the in the room uh with with Keelin as well. Like he's teaching all of the young guys like this how you work. this what you're supposed to do. This is what it looks like. And he loves those guys up, you know, sadly, well, not sadly, but just it is what it is. Our offensive line doesn't get all the love or appreciation even when they do good. Uh, but people are so quick to jump on their back when they're not doing great. And Trent does a good job by keeping those guys, you know, together. Um, you know, and making sure that they know that they're special football players. Um, he does the same thing for me. like even he don't got to say much but just his just his presence has really helped me to be more confident and you know he's been around some great quarterbacks in his career and and tells me that I'm like them in ways and better in other ways needs to work on this in other ways. So uh just really really a good vet. >> Oh go ahead. >> Hey CJ, uh speaking on your bye-week I saw you at the USC Ohio State game this past weekend. Obviously, not the outcome, you know, Buckeye would want, but what does it mean to you to just be back in a college football atmosphere and what do you think are their chances in the college football playoffs? >> Uh, yeah, it's cool always to come back. You know, it's different atmosphere, you know, a different swag, different little uh environment. So, um I thought it was cool, but honestly, it was just cool to see old coaches, old faces, you know, uh say what's up to the new guys um and really just talk to guys and just give them advice for the ones that want it or just really just be around. So, um, miss a lot of, you know, the times that I had with them. You know, got to talk to Coach Day and Coach Mick a bunch and that was really good for me and Coach Ke, all the different guys that I that I known when I was there that are still there. Um, but yeah, I mean, I think they have a great chance. You know, one thing that coach always preaches is fight. You know, it's never um it's never as bad as you seem or never as good as it it might seem. So, I believe that, you know, that culture there, we're built on toughness. Um, and you know, regardless of what that looks like or whoever is Ohio against the world and I'm proud of those guys, you know, regardless of win, lose or draw cuz I know the process and they keep the process going. Like I think they'll be fine. I think Luke Fehei is going to be a great quarterback, you know. I just love that room, too. They're all supporting one another. So, um, they got my support forever. See, there's 10 games left in the regular season and I know that you all are only trying to go one and0 um each week, but when you look at those 10 games and the way that you where you all are right now, do you still feel that the postseason is attainable for you all? >> We're focus on one thing at a time. I think, you know, this week was good for that. Um, and just really to check yourself like who are you, you know, and like what are you going to be, you know, like as the season goes on, you know, we drop some u some close games, but like doesn't mean like it's it's everything is is, you know, too far to reach, you know, but the best thing to do, like I just said, is focus on what's in front. Like we got meetings coming up in about an hour and those are just as important as, you know, when the ball snaps on Sunday. So, um, I think that's just got to be the focus because you go too far ahead, you can, you know, start losing track on the little things and those ultimately are the reasons why we haven't won, you know, those close games. So, focus on the little things and fix those and I think we'll be fine. >> All right. Yeah. All right.

title: Abraham Lucas: "All Of Our Running Backs Have Played Extremely Hard" | Seattle Seahawks
text: What was the conversation among the offensive line coming after Monday's game and evaluating overall play and and what happened? >> Um I mean, we took a look at it kind of as a group the film yesterday. Um and we just talked through kind of what we always talked through as far as like technique and you know, different looks and stuff that we saw there. I mean, I don't really know if there was like an super emotional official conversation. It's just kind of business as usual. >> Mike told us that Sam's not going this week and Drew will. What kind of confidence does an offense does it give you having seen Drew do what he's done this season and play so well? >> Uh Drew's always been a great quarterback. Um I mean, regardless of who they have or who we're blocking for uh utmost confidence in them. I mean um you know, I know Sam will take his rehab and Drew will step in and be the best version of himself for us. So, I got all the confidence in him. >> You've had a lot of different right guards next to you this season. Um how have you kind of done your best to help those guys all rotate in and now what are you doing with with to help Gray? >> Um I mean, it's just kind of a question of adapting to different styles of play, you know, I mean play next to what four guys this year. So, I mean that's just about adaptability, you know, I mean that that takes a little bit of time, you know, it's not a it's not an immediate just like easy flow type of thing, but you know, for Gray and myself it's just going to be learning each other's play styles as uh weeks and practices progress and get through and we'll you know, get to the point where we want to be, you know, we're both going to work hard at it and communicate with each other and kind of understand like what each other wants to do in certain situations and all of that and you know, Gray's a really bright guy, really smart, communicates really really well. So, uh we're on the right track, I would say. >> When it comes to play style, what does that cover? >> A play style meaning like um I mean, down and distance situationally, you know, if we're running I mean, if we have a chip front side, if we have help in the passing from the backfield or the tight end or um really the look on defense, you know, what I mean or the type of type of rusher that's on the edge in the three-tech. You know what I mean? So, there's a lot of like I mean, it's a process throughout the entire week, you know, it's not just a game day thing, but it's something that we work on the entire week, if that makes sense. >> How How much of that is about communication the run game coordination there again you feel how much of it's about picking up games and stunts and and stylistic stuff there? >> Um I mean, that's really what it's all about. I I mean, in kind of everything, right? I mean, there's no like I mean, it's 100% and 100% I would say. It's just about executing the play that's in front of you, you know, regardless of what the look is or what the play call is, you know. >> What Mike said Sam um cracked a rib on the second play of the game as well. Just him him playing through the rest of the game with all that what I guess that what does that what does that say about him to you guys? >> Oh, he's a tough son of a gun. I mean, I mean, a testament to who he is. I mean, he's always he's always been that way and you know, I don't think he gets enough credit for that toughness like physically and mentally, you know, I mean, hell of a quarterback and hell of a guy. Can't say enough good things about him. >> Mike mention or sorry, you just mentioned like se- the line watching the tape together. Your first look at Quinton Nelson playing with you guys like what what jumped out when you see his play? >> Um [snorts] I mean, Quinton Nelson is Quinton Nelson. I mean, he's you know, one of the best ever um to play and he brings a lot of a lot of knowledge and a lot of great um kind of gritty attitude towards the O-line and um I'd say he's fit in really well for only being here like 10 days. Um also a testament to how smart he is um you know, picking up an offense after three or four days and being able to go out and have the success that he had, so. >> The uh quarterback on the other side on Sunday someone that you know pretty well from Wazzu. Can you sort of encapsulate what Gardner meant to that program the one year that he was there in Pullman? >> Uh I mean, in my personal opinion, I just like I saw Gardner as a guy who you know, he came in kind of not really on a whim, but you know, Leach obviously recruited him and he came in and just was himself. He was totally who he was. He stayed true to himself and he had great success and he was the best version of himself uh throughout that entire year, you know, and we ended up having really good success with him and he's a hell of a guy, hell of a player. Um yeah, can't say enough great things about him. Uh I love to see him have success and be in the NFL as long as he's been and just continue to go till the wheels fall off, you know. Um you know, obviously want to beat him, >> [snorts] >> you know, this week, but um I'm just I'm happy for him. I love the guy. >> What was that year like? What was that again? Minshew Mania and all that and just the the buzz around him and the program? >> It was great. I mean, it was it was a I think it was just like a really complete year of team football for us. Um and I mean, he was kind of the superstar of that team, but he was also he didn't act like above anybody or anything like that. He was a consummate professional and a leader and it you know, is not a shock to me that he's still playing and and continuing to have the success that he's having just because that's always been who he is, you know. >> When it comes to the run game that you guys had on Monday night, could you feel the difference in the backs and having Zach back out there and having Price back out there? >> Um I mean, how do I answer this appropriately? I'm not I mean, all of our running backs have played extremely extremely hard and run extremely hard and have given us great opportunities for success. Um I mean, obviously Zach and JD are really good running backs and um happy to have them back in the fold, but that doesn't take away from what E-man and George have done, you know. So, I mean, I don't really I don't really look at it as like there was a difference per se. I mean, to me it's just business as usual, you know. Um I'm just trying to execute the blocks to give them the best chances for success. >> How much does it change your job when there's someone that's dedicated to a chip versus someone who's dedicated to stay in? Uh like how does that affect your your job on any individual play? >> I mean, it's just it's it's kind of just part of the part of the deal, you know? I mean, it's not like I don't I mean, I don't really know how to phrase it other than like it all is in all is part of the position, you know? It's not like a new thing, you know what I mean? It's something that we actively prepare for. While it may seem a little bit different maybe from the outside looking in like you know, we we pay special attention to these sorts of things and then like, you know, I mean, the game plan may change week to week, but that's all I mean, we know that that could possibly be changing if that makes sense. >> You used the phrase business as usual a couple times. Is Is that just sort of the approach you guys have right now despite I mean, obviously the record's not what you want it to be and things like that at this point of the year, but just kind of taking it that way? >> Well, sure. I mean, I don't I mean, you don't when things are don't happen the way you want to, you know, you don't just abandon your principles. I mean, that's a recipe for disaster, you know what I mean? It's like you have to hunker down on what you do. You have to hunker down on your process and and continue to commit to that even more hardcore regardless of the outcome, you know what I mean? I mean, you know, will you take a look at your process and probably tweak some things? I mean, sure, but you know, you don't just throw caution to the wind and re- reinvent the wheel, you know what I mean? So, yeah, it's just doubling down on what we do. >> You love working out in the off season as much as anybody. For the things you worked on this off season, how do you feel like those have translated so far this this year? I mean, I won't get into like the scientific [snorts] side of everything, but it's just like I mean, I feel I definitely feel like I'm stronger, you know, and able to stay healthier, um I guess more long-term. I mean, you guys know the history of my career just with the stuff, but um I mean, I feel good at this point. Um or about as good as you can feel after, you know, getting in a car wreck every Sunday. Um but yeah, I mean, it's definitely I mean, like you said, I love to work out and I think my commitment to that helps me long-term. >> Anything else? >> Thanks, Dave. >> Mhm. >> Dave. >> Thank you.

I don't want him to throw another interception on that play. So, I'm going to be a little more cautious with the football. And when you start being a little more cautious, you lose some of your aggressiveness. Aaron's always been a very aggressive passer. If someone was open down the field, he cut it loose. And I've been really impressed with Aaron this year because he was a very mobile quarterback for a long time. He could move in the top the pocket and buy a bunch of time. He doesn't quite have that same elusiveness and he's really transitioned to becoming more of a pocket passer. He's always been an incredible passer of the football, but now that he's playing from the pocket, he's totally in control. I think he's got like six interceptions this year. Five of them have been off the hands of his receivers or a Hail Mary. >> making incredible decisions. He always has made great decisions and you know, that's why that team's first place in their division and you know, I don't see anyone stopping him in that division, either. >> You know, it's like I want to circle back and wrap it with this. We had a lot of guys who we valued being very smart, and very tough. We tried to win every phase of the game. It wasn't like, ah kicking game, whatever, like what's happened with the Rams over the last couple years. >> We tried to win the kicking game. We invested in the kicking game. We had Matt Slater and one of the greatest special teamers in history. We had a great kicker, very good punter. We always had great special team schemes. Defensively, we essentially had Bill Belichick, you know, and Matt Patricia running that defense. We were always making that offense play left-handed. Now, they probably could have had they not had that defeatist mentality about them, but part of winning all that game all those games over the years, it puts some PTSD in our opponents as well. So yeah. >> Are there any places at this moment in time where you feel maybe not just all physically but emotionally too that you still want to improve? You still want to get better? >> Yeah. I think just continuing to give myself grace. It's been that's probably been the hardest thing for me prior to the injury. So now I think just definitely being patient with myself. It's been so long since I played. So continue to uh just show myself grace. >> That's interesting because I wanted I wanted to talk to you about the person you were before compared to the person you are now. I think emotionally matured as well. Um just out there playing lightly like um just having fun. I think that that'll be the difference between, you know, the years prior and now. >> There there's this whole like journey in your career because obviously you you you burst onto the scene as a freshman and maybe you didn't surprise yourself, but maybe you surprised other people and the expectations start to grow. I think just being really grounded in that um has definitely helped me, you know, just get over that pressure aspect of things. That's that's never the goal. I took for granted, you know, the little things in practice days I felt like st like super stressed. So definitely gives me perspective and to always cherish all the moments, good or bad. >> Okay, so you've got the season ahead of you now and obviously there are personal goals that you have, but there are also team goals. I think I couldn't I don't know if I can give you three. I think just very general of like getting better with my team. I'm a big like present person. I I like to take things each day at a time, but I think just continuing to grow as a team, rack up some dubs, and just be one of the last teams standing is is the goal. >> Okay.
